data.title: NB-UVB phototherapy — basics & targeted hand/foot units
data.summary: 311 nm UVB: indications, dosing logic and palmoplantar targeted units
data.body:
Narrowband UVB (NB-UVB) emits a peak at 311–313 nm. It is the first-line phototherapy for psoriasis and vitiligo. It is immunomodulatory and, in vitiligo, stimulates melanocytes. This SOP covers the principles and **targeted hand/foot units**; for cabin dosing see the Whole-body phototherapy SOP.

## Indications
- Psoriasis (plaque, guttate; palmoplantar with hand/foot units)
- Vitiligo (non-segmental, generalised or acrofacial)
- Atopic dermatitis, chronic hand eczema, prurigo
- Pruritus (uraemic, cholestatic), lichen planus, pityriasis rosea, PLEVA
- Early mycosis fungoides (patch stage)
- Polymorphic light eruption (prophylactic hardening)

## Contraindications
- Absolute: xeroderma pigmentosum, lupus erythematosus with photosensitivity, photosensitive genodermatoses
- Relative: history of melanoma or multiple NMSC, photosensitising drugs, prior arsenic or ionising radiation, immunosuppression (e.g. ciclosporin), cataract or aphakia, inability to stand or attend regularly, claustrophobia (cabin)
- Pregnancy: NB-UVB is acceptable; check folate status

## Pre-procedure
- Consent: needs 2–3 visits a week for months; erythema, tanning, itching; small long-term skin-cancer concern
- History of photosensitivity, drugs (doxycycline, NSAIDs, hydrochlorothiazide, fluoroquinolones, amiodarone), skin cancer
- Baseline: photographs, BSA/PASI or VASI; ANA if lupus is suspected
- Stop tar and avoid perfumes on treatment days; apply a thin layer of mineral oil on scaly psoriasis to improve penetration

## Equipment
- Calibrated NB-UVB unit with a UV meter; dose log book
- **Hand/foot unit**: a box with TL-01 tubes for palms and soles (and dorsa when the hands are turned)
- UV-protective goggles; cloth covers for uninvolved skin
- MED test template if MED-based dosing is used

## Procedure step by step (hand/foot unit)
1. Confirm the identity, the last dose and any erythema since the last session.
2. Remove rings and watches; cover the forearms and ankles with cloth.
3. Starting dose depends on the machine and the disease. Palms and soles tolerate higher doses because of their thick stratum corneum; start at the unit protocol dose (often about 0.3–0.5 J/cm²).
4. Treat palms, then dorsa (flip the hands); soles can be treated in the same or a separate unit.
5. Increase by 10–20% per session if there is no erythema or pain.
6. **Endpoint**: faint, painless erythema the next day; hold the dose if erythema is visible.
7. Record the dose, cumulative dose and any reaction in the log.

## Post-procedure care
- Emollients after each session; sunscreen on treated areas if going outdoors
- Avoid extra sun exposure on treatment days
- Continue topical steroid or calcipotriol in psoriasis, and topical calcineurin inhibitor in vitiligo, applied after the session

## Complications & management
- Erythema or burning: skip a session and restart at a lower dose
- Blisters: stop until healed, then restart at about 50% of the last dose
- Pruritus and xerosis: emollients
- Perilesional hyperpigmentation in vitiligo: reassure
- Flare of HSV or PLE: treat and adjust

## Sessions & follow-up
- 2–3 times a week on non-consecutive days
- Psoriasis: clearance usually in 20–30 sessions; vitiligo: first repigmentation at 2–3 months and assess at 6 months
- Stop if there is no response at 6 months (vitiligo) or ~30 sessions (psoriasis)
- Annual skin check with long courses
